stem: A nurse is preparing the family caregiver of a client with residual deficits after stroke for discharge home. Which teaching plan best aligns with American Heart Association/American Stroke Association recommendations for caregiver support?

options.A: Use an individualized plan that combines practical skill-building with psychoeducational support and reassess caregiver needs after discharge.
options.B: Provide a standardized written packet focused on stroke facts and defer practical skills training until home services begin.
options.C: Limit teaching to psychoeducation during hospitalization because practical skills are best learned only after discharge.
options.D: Teach only the client unless the caregiver requests training, then provide the same material used for all families.

rationale: The AHA/ASA stroke rehabilitation guideline recommends caregiver interventions that combine skill building with psychoeducational strategies, are tailored to the individual caregiver's needs, and include postdischarge assessment with interventions adjusted as needs change. Therefore, option A is the best plan. A standardized information-only approach (B), psychoeducation without skill building (C), and client-only or one-size-fits-all caregiver teaching (D) do not match these recommendations.
educational_objective: Select an individualized post-stroke caregiver education plan that combines practical skill-building with psychoeducational support and includes reassessment after discharge as caregiver needs change.
source_document_title: Guidelines for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery: A Guideline for Healthcare Professionals From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
source_locator: Transitions in Care and Community Rehabilitation → Ensuring Medical and Rehabilitation Continuity Through the Rehabilitation Process and Into the Community; paragraph summarizing Class I caregiver/dyad intervention recommendations: combine skill building with psychoeducational strategies, tailor interventions to caregiver needs, and perform postdischarge assessments with tailored interventions based on changing needs.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports individualized stroke caregiver interventions combining skill-building and psychoeducational strategies, plus postdischarge reassessment and tailoring to changing caregiver needs. Currentness was cross-checked against the AHA/ASA 2025 rehabilitation access policy statement and the 2026 acute ischemic stroke guideline, which continue to reference the adult stroke rehabilitation guideline for poststroke rehabilitation practice.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A → Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care → Case Management, PDF page 20 (file page 23): plan individualized care based on need and provide information on discharge procedures to home or community setting.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized discharge planning/caregiver preparation for transition to home
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item. The original answer bundled broad claims about warning signs and community resources under a generic heart.org locator that did not directly support every asserted component. The revised item tests a narrower, explicitly sourced AHA/ASA caregiver-intervention recommendation and removes unsupported precision and generic distractors.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Post-stroke discharge planning and family caregiver education
audit_findings.source_authority: Primary specialty guidance from AHA/ASA; no secondary clinical source used for the decisive claim.
audit_findings.currentness: The 2016 adult stroke rehabilitation guideline remains the AHA/ASA detailed rehabilitation reference; AHA/ASA publications in 2025 and 2026 continue to direct readers to it for poststroke rehabilitation practice.

claim_by_claim.stem: Residual post-stroke deficits and discharge-home caregiver preparation are clinically coherent with the guideline's transitions-of-care section.
claim_by_claim.A: Directly matches the guideline's combined skill-building plus psychoeducational approach, individualized tailoring, and postdischarge reassessment.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because a standardized information-only plan omits individualized skill-building and intentionally defers the practical component.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because the guideline favors skill-building combined with psychoeducational strategies rather than psychoeducation alone.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because caregiver education/support is recommended and tailored caregiver interventions are preferred over one-size-fits-all approaches.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Contains only claims traceable to the cited caregiver/dyad recommendations and does not introduce unsourced numerical thresholds or universal rules.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to selection of an evidence-aligned caregiver teaching plan for transition home after stroke.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B, C, and D are clinically plausible teaching errors but each conflicts with a distinct cited recommendation; none is absurd or an alternative best answer.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A contains all three decisive evidence-based elements: skill-building plus psychoeducation, individual tailoring, and postdischarge reassessment. No second defensible answer remains.
audit_findings.cueing: Choice lengths and wording were reviewed; no grammatical keying, absolute-word giveaway, or duplicate/overlapping alternatives identified.
audit_findings.blueprint: Mapped to 2026 NCLEX-RN Management of Care because the item requires selecting individualized discharge/care-transition teaching for home care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-read without relying on the original key; challenged each option as a possible best answer, rechecked the decisive AHA/ASA recommendations and NCSBN classification, and found no unresolved clinical, source, locator, ambiguity, or cueing conflict.
